model: Demucs v4 htdemucs_6s (Hybrid Transformer Demucs, 6 parts: drums, bass, other, vocals, guitar, piano)
authors: Alexandre Défossez, Simon Rouard and contributors, Meta AI Research
licence: MIT (LICENSE-demucs.txt, the Demucs repository licence; the repository gives no separate licence for its pretrained weights)
conversion: The network part of HTDemucs.forward (between the spectrogram and the inverse spectrogram, so the graph has no complex numbers) was exported with torch.onnx.export (torch 2.5.1, opset 17, legacy exporter). Inputs: mix [1,2,343980] and the complex-as-channels spectrogram [1,4,2048,336]; outputs: the 6 parts' spectrograms [1,6,4,2048,336] and time branches [1,6,2,343980].

Weights are stored as float16 with a Cast back to float32 (onnx 1.23.2), so the download is half the size while the computation stays float32. Checked against PyTorch on a real song segment: max difference 0.00018 (spectrogram, rms 0.16) and 0.00004 (time branch, rms 0.23).
The spectrogram, inverse spectrogram, song normalisation and 25 % overlapping segments run in JavaScript (src/separation/demucs.ts), as in demucs.apply_model with shifts = 0.
Made by scripts/separation/export-model.py; a rebuild on 2026-10-15 gave the same file byte for byte.
notes: Demucs' own documentation calls the piano part of htdemucs_6s weak. The split is done on the user's device; no audio is uploaded.
